To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a new methodological framework to estimate the carbon balance of selective tropical managed forests, and that the net balance of selective logging over 38 years in French Guiana is comprised between 0 and 1.3 Tg C.

we propose an innovating framework to assess the above-ground carbon fluxes from managed tropical forests, based on logging statistics, which allows the estimation of the carbon balance of a managed forest estate at a regional scale.
“The net carbon balance of tropical selective logging is estimated between -0.12 and +1.33 Teg C year-1 with a median value of +0.64 Teg C Year-1 for the French Guianese Permanent Forest Estate.”
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods for estimating the carbon budget of tropical production forests.
the development of a methodological framework to quantify the carbon budget of tropical forests.

a major issue of the 21st century: to provide a robust and transparent framework for carbon accounting of tropical forests, in order to contribute to the mitigation of global change and the implementation of REDD+.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
selective logging in French Guiana has a small net carbon sink effect.
selective logging of tropical forests in French Guiana is not carbon neutral, with a median carbon sink of 0.65 Tg C over 38 years, but the net carbon balance is highly uncertain.
logging is carbon negative in French Guiana.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our methodological framework provides a useful approach to assess carbon budget of tropical selective logging.
the above-ground carbon stock of selectively logged forests remains positive after logging, but with a large range of uncertainty.
the above-ground carbon stock is the main determinant of the carbon budget of managed forests.
The main takeaway from our work is that
selective logging in the humid tropic is carbon-neutral, but the uncertainty on the net balance is large and could be reduced by improved knowledge of the fate of logging damage.
the above-ground carbon stock in selectively logged forests is not a static variable.
selective logging is not necessarily carbon negative in the humid tropic, but the carbon budget is highly dependent on the management practices.
